wikidata.note: agent-checked 2026-10-25 (travel-researcher): Wikidata label 'Montmorency Falls', instance of waterfall, P625 within 0.1 km of OSM node 1199354691 'Chute Montmorency'; needs a person's check

draw.note: Visiter Québec, the Québec City tourism board, headlines the falls as a destination 'you will not want to miss'; Sépaq-managed park.

standing.note: The 83 m fall is the region's best-known waterfall (tourism board listing).

distinction.note: 83 m, 30 m taller than Niagara Falls (tourism board listing); Canyon Sainte-Anne's 74 m fall is the nearest comparable.

easy_payoff.note: Seen from the belvedere and bridge at the top of the falls; OSM maps a belvedere 70 m from the falls.

weather.note: The listing says it is as spectacular in winter as in summer.

records.why: An 83 m waterfall, 30 m higher than Niagara, 15 minutes from Old Québec.

access_cost.note: No permit or booking to see the falls. Parking: free outdoor lots and paid outdoor lots (Visiter Québec). Cable car and activities are sold separately.

designations.note: No designation of its own found on the pages read for this place.

draw.note: Visiter Québec (the tourism board) lists it as a must-see near Québec City; the operator headlines a 74 m waterfall and three suspension bridges.

standing.note: A paid, managed canyon park with a 74 m fall; the nearer Montmorency Falls is the bigger name.

distinction.note: A 74 m fall with a 60 m suspension bridge over the gorge (operator page).

easy_payoff.note: The fall and bridges need the 2.2 km Canyon Trail down into the gorge; there is no roadside view.

weather.note: Open air with railed lookouts; opens in rain.

records.why: A 74 m waterfall and three suspension bridges over a Canadian Shield canyon, 35 minutes from Old Québec.

access_cost.note: Paid admission 2026: adult CAD 15, age 6 to 17 CAD 10, 5 and under free; no booking needed (online tickets optional); parking free (operator pages).

designations.note: No designation of its own found on the pages read for this place.

wikidata.note: agent-checked 2026-10-25 (travel-researcher): Q3224379 is Le Massif, the ski resort (P625 47.28,-70.61); there is no item for the lookout itself, so the resort is the parent item

draw.note: Operator headline: Le Massif's signature lookout with a 360-degree view; no tourism board listing was read.

standing.note: The resort's own signature lookout.

distinction.note: A 30 m man-made mound; Charlevoix has other summit and coast viewpoints.

easy_payoff.note: A 2 km easy loop from the summit parking; the resort says the lookout is near the summit lot.

records.why: A 30 m viewing mound at the summit of Le Massif with a 360-degree view over Charlevoix and the St. Lawrence.

access_cost.note: Hiking trails are free (operator); the gondola is optional and paid (CAD 33 adult in 2026); no booking.

draw.note: Inside Forillon National Park (national park designation, parent); Parks Canada's hiking page names it as a trailhead.

standing.note: A named cape and trailhead of the park.

distinction.note: Forillon has several capes and lookouts; not compared further.

easy_payoff.note: Distance from the car park to the viewing point is not stated.

records.why: A sea-cliff cape in Forillon National Park and the start of the Mont-Saint-Alban climb.

access_cost.note: Park admission applies (adult CAD 10 in peak season 2026, 7.25 shoulder; youth free); no permit or booking.

draw.note: Inside Forillon National Park (national park designation, parent); the Parks Canada hiking page headlines the lighthouse and Land's End at the cape.

standing.note: The end of the park's main coastal trail and the tip of the peninsula.

distinction.note: Land's End, the end of the International Appalachian Trail in Forillon (park page).

easy_payoff.note: No road to the cape: the Les Graves walk is 6.4 km round trip on the gravel road or 8 km on the trail.

records.why: The tip of the Gaspé Peninsula: a lighthouse on a 95 m cliff and Land's End, reached on foot in Forillon.

v.note: 6.4 km round trip on the gravel road (172 m gain) or 8 km on the trail (310 m gain)

access_cost.note: Park admission applies on top of the walk.

draw.note: Parks Canada designated it a heritage lighthouse on 28 January 2026 (official designation).

standing.note: A designated heritage lighthouse on the Gaspé coast road.

distinction.note: Lighthouses are common along the St. Lawrence coast; not compared further.

easy_payoff.note: The tower is seen from the coast road and the adjacent belvedere (OSM maps one 0.14 km away).

records.why: A red octagonal lighthouse of 1906 on the St. Lawrence, designated a heritage lighthouse in 2026.

access_cost.note: No permit or booking found; opening dates and any admission fee for the museum were not found.

standing.note: A named lake on the park's trail network below Mont Xalibu.

distinction.note: The park has other named lakes; not compared further.

easy_payoff.note: On foot from the 40-place car park; the lake is at least 1.6 km away in a straight line.

records.why: A lake under Mont Xalibu in Parc national de la Gaspésie, reached on foot from a 40-place car park.

v.note: on foot from the car park; the Mont Xalibu route beyond it is open only 1 July to 30 September

draw.note: Bonjour Québec (the provincial tourism board) lists it; the operator headlines Québec's highest suspension footbridge.

standing.note: Named by the tourism board as a must for nature lovers in the region.

distinction.note: A 5 km river canyon with walls up to 90 m and the highest suspension footbridge in Québec (operator pages).

easy_payoff.note: Trails of more than 20 km lead to the footbridge and falls; the Descente aux Enfers staircase is closed after a rockfall.

records.why: A 5 km river canyon with walls up to 90 m, the Grand Sault falls and Québec's highest suspension footbridge.

access_cost.note: Paid day access 2026: adult CAD 17.80, age 5 to 17 CAD 9.92, family CAD 49.34, 4 and under free (taxes extra); immersive trails extra; free Accès nature day tickets exist on request-limited reservation. Parking free.

draw.note: Inside Parc national de la Gaspésie (provincial park designation, parent); Rando Québec calls its panorama one of the best in the park.

standing.note: Named by Rando Québec as one of the park's best panoramas.

distinction.note: Woodland caribou habitat: the route is closed outside 1 July to 30 September to protect them (Rando Québec).

easy_payoff.note: An 11.4 km return hike with 648 m gain, 5 to 6 hours.

records.why: A 1,120 m summit with tundra panoramas and woodland caribou habitat, open 1 July to 30 September.

v.note: route open only 1 July to 30 September (caribou protection); dogs banned

standing.note: The highest summit of the south-shore estuary region (Rando Québec).

distinction.note: The highest summit of its natural region, with a view over the estuary islands (Rando Québec).

easy_payoff.note: A 7.7 km return trail with 370 m gain, about 4 hours.

records.why: The highest summit of the south-shore estuary region, via a 7.7 km return trail in Parc national du Bic.

draw.note: Operator headline: the village's cooperative sells the 'Station de montagne sur mer' with a summit observatory, a shuttle and tandem free flights.

standing.note: A small coastal village built around a 430 m mountain station.

distinction.note: A free-flight (hang-gliding and paragliding) site on the Gaspé coast; the cooperative offers tandem flights.

easy_payoff.note: The village centre and the church-hall show are on the main road.

weather.note: Indoor shows exist; the summit and flights depend on weather.

records.why: A Gaspé coast village under a 430 m mountain: free-flight launch, summit observatory, shuttle and year-round trails.

access_cost.note: Summit by shuttle or on foot; paid access and shows (rates on the operator's pages, not read); no booking needed to walk the village.

draw.note: Inside Parc national de l'Île-Bonaventure-et-du-Rocher-Percé (provincial park designation); Rando Québec's sheet headlines the most accessible northern gannet colony.

standing.note: The sheet describes it as the most accessible northern gannet colony in the world.

distinction.note: A colony of about 110,000 nesting birds (Rando Québec sheet).

easy_payoff.note: Boat from Percé, then an 8.4 km loop of about 3 hours; the sheet gives no shorter route.

weather.note: Boat sailings and the colony depend on sea and sky.

records.why: An island park with a northern gannet colony of about 110,000 birds, reached by boat from Percé.

v.note: boats leave from the Percé quay; access depends on sea conditions

access_cost.note: Park access is paid (free for under 18); the boat is a separate ticket (operator pages not read).

standing.note: The best-known landmark of the peninsula.

records.why: An 88 m rock with a natural arch off Percé, the best-known landmark of the Gaspé Peninsula.

access_cost.note: Seen from the shore with no permit; boat cruises around the rock run from the quay (operator pages not read).
